plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do. This ensures you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (maximizing profit) and never overpay (never lose money) when you do win. Since payment equals the second-highest bid, not my own bid, there's no benefit to shading below value. I'll bid exactly my value of $31.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit: if I bid below value, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won; if I bid above value, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value. With value $37, I'll bid exactly $37.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' behavior. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above value risks negative profit, and bidding below value only reduces chances of winning profitable auctions. With a value of $11, I should bid exactly $11 to maximize expected profit.
